To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the first-order incremental query language is expressive enough to compute all first-order queries; (2) the first-order language can be extended to handle queries with negation; (3) first-order incremental evaluation can be performed using a bottom-up evaluation strategy, and (4) the incremental evaluation can be implemented using a single scan of the database, and thus is very efficient.

(1) first-order incremental query processing is a powerful tool that can be applied to many different types of queries, and (2) it can be implemented efficiently, using only the database and query evaluation techniques that are already available in most database systems.
(1) first-order incremental query processing is feasible and (2) first-order incremental processing can be used to improve the efficiency of query evaluation in some situations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the complexity of first-order incremental query eval- uation, and what can we say about its performance?
the following questions: (1) How much can be saved by incremental query evaluation?
the following questions: (1) What are the computational and space requirements of first-order incremental query computation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

first-order incremental query processing is not feasible for the evaluation of recursive queries, and that first-order incremental evaluation of nonrecursive queries is not feasible for queries with arbitrary predicates and relations.
first-order incremental query processing is a viable alternative to the more traditional approach of recomputing queries from scratch, especially for queries that are expensive to evaluate.
the problem of first-order incremental evaluation of Datalog queries has not yet been solved, but the work reported here represents an important step towards a solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that first-order incremental query evalution is feasible, that it is useful, and that it is practical.
first-order incremental evaluation is a powerful technique for speeding up repeated query evaluation.
incremental evaluation of first-order queries is possible in polynomial time, but that the complexity of the problem is still open for queries with recursion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for many classes of queries, first-order incremental query computation can be implemented efficiently and can achieve substantial speedups over the cost of computing the query from scratch each time.
, in the context of first-order incremental query processing, the choice of the query evaluation algorithm has a significant impact on the efficiency of the process.
first-order incremental evaluation can significantly reduce the cost of repeated query evaluation.
